highlights_headline: The upcoming SkiaSharp 4.156.0 release improves rendering reliability and updates Apple and Uno platform requirements.
highlights_body: Android texture rendering follows display refresh, Windows custom fonts release their backing data correctly, and Linux HarfBuzz avoids conflicts with system libraries. Same-milestone Skia fixes improve shader handling and Graphite rendering.

breaking.title: Update Apple deployment targets
breaking.body: SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp native libraries now require macOS 12 or iOS, tvOS and Mac Catalyst 15. Raise application deployment targets accordingly, retaining any higher framework requirements. These final floors supersede the earlier macOS 11 and iOS/tvOS/Catalyst 14 native baselines and support Xcode 27 builds; .NET 9 targets remain available.

breaking.title: Move Uno applications to Uno Platform 7
breaking.body: The non-Windows Uno views now require Uno 7 and .NET 10; pre-Uno 7 WasmShell pipelines are no longer supported. Migrate to Uno.Sdk's .NET SDK WebAssembly path. SKSwapChainPanel now derives from Grid, drops RaiseOnUnsupported and uses a CPU canvas with null GRContext on non-Windows Uno. Use SKCanvasElement for GPU drawing there. The Windows App SDK facade remains ANGLE-backed.

breaking.title: Rebuild custom WebAssembly archives for WebGPU linking
breaking.body: Newer WebAssembly consumers expect emdawnwebgpu's C++ support inside libSkiaSharp.a rather than compiling it during application linking. Use matching rebuilt native assets; old archives and GPU-disabled custom archives do not meet that contract. The .NET 8 built-in WebGPU link path is retained.

breaking.title: Replace the fork-specific WinRT native target
breaking.body: The fork-specific WinRT native target has been retired. Consumers of that target must move to a supported Windows target. Desktop Windows, WinUI/Windows App SDK and NanoServer remain supported.

bullets.detail: Same-milestone m156 updates reject overflowing SkSL slot counts and invalid runtime-effect types, prevent undersized conic-region buffers, and stop partially constructed runtime-shader pipelines from executing.

bullets.lead: Graphite stroke bounds and paint keys corrected
bullets.detail: Hairline and subpixel stroke bounds include cap and join inflation, while paint-key comparisons examine the complete key rather than only a prefix.
Disables the BGRA8-as-RGBx upload configuration that advertised GL_RGBA but was invalid in GLES. Readback behavior is unchanged.

Automatic continuous GLTextureView rendering, including MAUI Android SKGLView.HasRenderLoop, follows display callbacks instead of running at buffer-swap throughput. Drawing stays on the GL worker; explicit render requests and WhenDirty behavior are preserved.

Skia callbacks use one-byte native booleans and HarfBuzz callbacks use four-byte hb_bool_t values, fixing ABI mismatches including Apple ARM64 interpreter returns. Public managed callbacks still use bool; failed HarfBuzz glyph-name callbacks no longer copy a name.

Bundled HarfBuzz calls bind to their own implementation, preventing incompatible private objects from crossing into system HarfBuzz after libraries such as GTK load it globally. Exported entry points and managed signatures are unchanged.

bullets.lead: Text-buffer validation and string decoding corrected
bullets.detail: Negative encoded-text lengths now throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException; odd GlyphID byte counts throw ArgumentException. StringUtilities decodes single-unit character codes by encoding width: use UTF-32 for supplementary code points. GetString now reports null byte arrays with ArgumentNullException. FromCString also fixes a native buffer over-read.

bullets.lead: Windows font and view resources released correctly
bullets.detail: DWriteCore custom-font data is released after the last dependent typeface clone is disposed, while remaining usable by live clones. WinUI GL view teardown unbinds its own current EGL context before destroying the surface so the native window can be released.
Retains the OpenGL module behind cached WGL pointers and corrects optional stream callbacks and XPS COM ownership. Also corrects front-buffered stream retention.

Valid managed pixel copies avoid an intermediate SKData allocation. HarfBuzzSharp AddUtf32 string calls avoid allocating an encoded byte array each time, and feature-string conversion avoids a native allocation while preserving existing decoding behavior.
The Windows library baseline moves to Windows App SDK 1.7.250909003, and bundled WinUI ANGLE advances to chromium/8118. These updates do not change the declared Windows runtime minimum.

bullets.lead: Portable Windows runtime identifiers in source builds
bullets.detail: AnyCPU native imports for SkiaSharp, HarfBuzzSharp and WinUI now select architecture-specific assets for win-x86, win-x64 and win-arm64 instead of legacy win10-* identifiers. Explicit-platform and empty-RID selection paths remain unchanged.

bullets.lead: WebAssembly application links no longer compile WebGPU C++ support
bullets.detail: Moving emdawnwebgpu's C++ support into the native archive avoids passing C++20 flags to application C sources. Required JavaScript glue remains a link input rather than deployed application content.
